what: Measured reproduction of the single-worker API deadlock found by the release gate, before and after the bounded SQLite pool fix in Adapt-main/backend/src/adapt/db/engine.py.
method: A fresh uvicorn process (ADAPT_DB_ENCRYPTION=field-only, ADAPT_RATE_LIMIT_MULTIPLIER=60, external resource providers disabled) per concurrency level; one guest learner; N simultaneous POST /api/v1/explain requests with an explicit 6 s client timeout; then GET /healthz with a 3 s timeout. Same host, same interpreter, same code except the pool configuration.

before_fix.engine_pool: SQLAlchemy default QueuePool for file SQLite (size 5, max_overflow 10, pool_timeout 30)
before_fix.additional_observation: With external providers left enabled, 16 concurrent requests produced 3 x 200 in ~110 ms, 13 x timeout at 40 s, and /healthz then timed out at 8 s. The first three requests had already entered the awaited resource lookup; later ones blocked on SQLite connection checkout.

after_fix.engine_pool: explicit QueuePool (size 20, max_overflow 20, pool_timeout 5, pool_pre_ping true) for file databases; in-memory databases keep SingletonThreadPool

interpretation: The defect was connection-pool starvation, not an AI credential or provider issue. It is fixed by a bounded, explicit pool and pinned by backend/tests/test_release_concurrency_pool.py plus the live concurrency scenario in release/stress_check.py. These numbers are a single-machine loopback measurement, not a capacity guarantee.
